notes: PROD PROMOTION #2 (2026-09-01, COMBINED IMAGE): prod.tag -> 2026.8.1-isol8.2-035a60f, matching dev, digest sha256:0a860792108138c3ad8c46caf44338211250fb5f33a3c283bc30edf12d2cb2d4, built from main 035a60fc3. This ONE image carries three legs that must ship together: the stable-8.1 base (upstream v2026.8.1 + our 15 carried patches), #2275's lightbulb-connect.sh / lightbulb-api.sh skill scripts, and #2241's isol8 -> lightbulb runtime-identifier rename. Built as a single image DELIBERATELY -- #2241 carries image content (Dockerfile, the local-sqlite boot script, the baked aws-exec-profile plugin, skills/lightbulb/SKILL.md), so pinning the intermediate -6e65834 first would have forced a SECOND reroll of all 28 containers. #2241 also changes core/containers/config.py, the config emitter, so image and backend must land together: a reroll straddling them would provision a config the booted image does not expect. GATED ON A REAL DEV BOOT, not just artifact checks. Four independent checks agreed the artifact was correct (image-layer content read, plus three matching digest reads) and NONE of them proved it boots -- #2241's rename has NO fallback, so if the boot script's read path and config.py's write path disagree on lightbulb-facts.json the container crash-loops. An earlier PR that flipped BOTH pins straight to this image was CLOSED for exactly that reason: its own notes documented a -d60978a validation while flipping prod to -035a60f. So dev.tag went first (#2283), a dev container was reprovisioned to take its FIRST boot on -035a60f, and two sessions verified independently -- gateway_healthy + the 8.1 agents.entries config shape, and lightbulb-facts.json present with zero isol8- residue at runtime. Takes effect on the next prod workflow_dispatch of deploy.yml; existing per-user containers keep their own task-def revision until rolled. SUPERSEDES -d60978a, which was prod's pin for ~1h and never reached a single running container. FIELD MEANINGS (read before bumping anything): `upstream` is the fork base the Dockerfile FROMs -- a PRIVATE GHCR package pulled only by the authenticated build workflow; keep it in lockstep with apps/infra/openclaw/Dockerfile's FROM line, which is hardcoded and has no build-arg templating. `image`/`tag`/`full` are the LEGACY PUBLIC upstream image, kept only as the bootstrap/unknown-env fallback in container-stack.ts (pulled by per-user ECS tasks with NO registry credentials, so it must stay anonymously pullable). `extendedImage` + per-env dev.tag/prod.tag are the ECR extended image actually deployed; dev.tag/prod.tag are the per-environment promotion gate (flip dev, validate, then prod). STABLE 8.1 BASE BUMP (2026-09-01): see git history for tag v2026.8.1-isol8.2 and PR #2270 -- upstream cut stable v2026.8.1 on 2026-08-30, 3,311 commits after the beta.3 we were running; the window carries the SQLite split-brain WAL fix (#132844), shared-filesystem rollback journaling (#120597), newer-state refusal (#132916/#133081), the large-session + Doctor perf set, and the low-memory postinstall fix. DEV VALIDATION THAT GATED THIS PROMOTION (2026-09-01, owner user_3IeOW2y8Y1o84mB2dnxZ54Ok9Xp): the account was wiped to nothing via DELETE /debug/user-data, then onboarded end-to-end through the real UI. The container provisioned onto this image (task-def lightbulb-dev-openclaw-user:17), reaching RUNNING + gateway_healthy in ~30s, far inside doctor's 300s budget. Friday AND Atlas both seeded, and openclaw.json came out in the 8.1 agents.entries MAP shape -- confirming the config shape gate on the stable base. Verified INSIDE the live container, not just in unit tests: skills.workshop.autonomous.mode=off, agents.defaults.maxConcurrent=4, memory.search.rememberAcrossConversations=false, heartbeat every=0m. A real agent run streamed a reply; the browser live-view panel rendered; teams_state=active; trial spend stayed 0; the trial park -> wake cycle worked. KNOWN GAP, DELIBERATELY ACCEPTED: the model-picker behaviour this line was originally chosen for (upstream #115953 -- full-discovery escalation on an agents.defaults.modelPolicy.allow provider wildcard) is NOT active, because the backend emits no modelPolicy at all. modelCatalogBrowseRequiresFullDiscovery returns false with zero provider wildcards, so a ChatGPT-OAuth owner's picker still resolves against the static plugin manifest and can still be offered gpt-5.5-pro. Fixing that needs a follow-up config change emitting agents.defaults.modelPolicy.allow -- NOT agents.defaults.models, which is the LEGACY path and only escalates the 'configured' view, never the 'default' view the picker sends (src/agents/model-catalog-browse.ts). This promotion therefore rests on the fixes independent of the picker: SQLite split-brain WAL corruption (#132844), shared-filesystem rollback journaling (#120597), newer-state refusal (#132916/#133081), the large-session + Doctor perf set, and the low-memory postinstall fix (#132555). STILL UNMEASURED: a MULTI-AGENT tenant's boot against doctor's 300s budget -- the dev canary had 2 agents, not the 11+ that crash-looped in 2026-08. PRIOR NOTES for the beta.3 line are in git history for tag v2026.8.1-isol8.1.
